data.outcome_summary: This OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note summarizes adult proficiency in Israel across three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—using adults aged 16–65 assessed in 2022–23. It reports mean proficiency on 500-point scales and the distribution across proficiency levels (e.g., shares at Level 1 or below and at Levels 4–5), alongside uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals). The note also documents subgroup differences by age (older adults scoring lower than younger adults), and compares trends over time between 2014–15 and 2022–23, including a decline in literacy and stable numeracy. Beyond skills, it reports associations between higher numeracy proficiency and labour force participation, and between higher proficiency levels and well-being/civic outcomes, as well as qualification/skills mismatches for employed adults. The excerpt does not provide model-based ML methods or explicit PV/missing-data handling details, so the results should be interpreted as survey-based descriptive and regression-adjusted relationships reported by OECD rather than as outputs from an ML prediction pipeline.
